key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize building energy management by lowering electricity costs while making battery-control decisions interpretable.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports practical, trustable control of PV-equipped buildings with batteries under dynamic prices, forecasts, and real-world operating conditions.
method: Train on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for residential building energy control.
Use an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, electricity price, weather, calendar, holiday, and forecast inputs.
Apply post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned policies.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates both synthetic data and real-world LLEC (KIT) data and reports that A2C and PPO outperform off-policy methods in cumulative reward and policy stability.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on high-quality forecasts and time-varying measurements, deployment may be sensitive to data errors or sensor/forecast drift.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
